+decisions:
+  - id: OR-1
+    gates: true
+    title: Which figures may feed a determination for a group of people?
+    question: "Should a figure reach a determination only through the lens tags written on that figure, and never through the crossing maps between identity groups, ICF codes and needs?"
+    why_yours: "Decision D-0184 says yes and is adopted with review pending, waiting for you. It is a rule about how evidence reaches people, which is doctrine."
+    context: |-
+      Every figure the project reads from a source is tagged with who it applies to: an identity group, an ICF function code, an access need, a medical condition. A determination is built for one parameter and one lens, for example 'running slope, wheelchair users'.
+
+      D-0184 says a figure counts for a lens only if that lens is written on the figure itself. The alternative walks the crossing maps (identity to ICF to need) to decide which figures apply. D-0184 measured that traversal and rejected it, because it pulls in figures that do not apply.
+
+      In practice, determinations of slope for autistic people, blind people, ADHD, an ICF movement code (d450) and an effort need have no figures written for them yet. Each would read 'pending', with a gap naming the missing lens, instead of borrowing the wheelchair-user figures.
+    blocks: "The lens-routing change (T-3) and lens tagging of existing rows (D-2)."
+    options:
+      - key: "yes"
+        label: "Yes, only the lens tags on the figure"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "T-3 is built as written. Those five determinations read 'pending' with a gap that names the lens. Unblocks T-3 and D-2."
+      - key: "no"
+        label: "No, use the crossing maps"
+        effect: "You state the traversal rule in your own words. D-0184 is recorded as superseded. T-3 then builds the walk over the identity, ICF and need maps, which is more code and the traversal D-0184 rejected."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-1); workplan section 4"

+  - id: OR-1b
+    gates: false
+    title: Does a figure tagged for everyone ('ALL') apply to every group?
+    question: "Should a figure tagged with the identity code ALL reach the determination of every identity group?"
+    why_yours: "It decides whether a statement about everyone counts as evidence about each group."
+    context: |-
+      Some figures carry the identity code ALL. It is a scope marker: the source speaks to everyone, not to a particular group.
+
+      If ALL figures reached every group, a determination for blind people could rest on a figure that was never about blind people. The page would then have to say the value is a statement of scope, not evidence about that group.
+    blocks: "The lens-routing change (T-3)."
+    options:
+      - key: "no"
+        label: "No, ALL reaches only an ALL determination"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "ALL figures are used only for a determination whose lens is ALL."

+  - id: OR-2
+    gates: true
+    title: How is a conditional claim shown?
+    question: "Should a determination show conditional claims as branches beside a headline taken only from unconditioned claims, leaving the headline empty when every claim is conditioned?"
+    why_yours: "It changes what a reader sees for a parameter, and the alternatives trade strictness against readability."
+    context: |-
+      A source may state a figure only under a condition, for example 'a steeper slope is allowed if the ramp is under one metre'. Today a code's step table prints as one number, so the condition disappears.
+
+      The proposal keeps each conditional claim as its own branch, shown beside the headline. The headline comes only from claims with no condition. If every claim has a condition, the headline is empty and the branches are all that is shown.
+    blocks: "The conditions change (T-2) and the repair of parameter 3's rows (D-1)."
+    options:
+      - key: branches-empty-headline
+        label: "Branches, and an empty headline when all are conditioned"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "T-2 is built as written."
+      - key: strictest-branch
+        label: "Branches, and the strictest branch as headline when all are conditioned"
+        effect: "T-2 composes the headline from all governing rows when none is unconditioned, and the note says so."

+  - id: OR-3

+    title: May a stored figure be reformatted in place?

+    blocks: "The repair of parameter 3's rows (D-1), and the widening of the amend verb (T-1 step 8)."

+      - key: "yes"

+    title: May a figure read in full but not yet reviewed set a value?
+    question: "May a figure read in full but still 'preliminary' (not reviewed) set a published value?"
+    why_yours: "It has been open since 2026-10-09 and the code's own comment forbids deciding it without you."
+    context: |-
+      A figure read from the whole text can still carry the status 'preliminary' because nobody has reviewed it. The question is whether that is enough to set a published value, with a flag.
+    blocks: "The flag in the renderer (T-5)."
+    options:
+      - key: yes-flagged
+        label: "Yes, flagged"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "No engine change. The renderer flags 'preliminary' rows."
+      - key: "no"
+        label: "No"
+        effect: "Add 'preliminary' to the rule beside the not-publishable methods. The comment there forbids doing that without this answer. It adds a line of code that no work item owns yet."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-11b); workplan section 4"

+    title: Scope four languages out until buckets 1 and 2 are exhausted?
+    question: "Are Arabic, Bengali, Hindi and Swahili, which the language-to-jurisdiction map requires and which have no aliases, scoped out by the bucket table until buckets 1 and 2 are exhausted?"

+        effect: "They wait behind buckets 1 and 2."

+        label: "No, build aliases now"

+    title: May a model-generated alias be used if the search is flagged?
+    question: "May an alias that a model generated be used for a search, if the search is flagged as using it?"
+    why_yours: "It concerns the provenance of search terms."

+      Some search aliases were generated by a model rather than taken from a source. `python3 scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py` lists them.

+
+  - id: OR-13
+    gates: false
+    title: Seed the list of quantities from the codes already held, or topic by topic?
+    question: "Should the quantity list be seeded by an open-pass scan of the bucket 1 and 2 codes already held, rather than slug by slug?"
+    why_yours: "It was left open on 2026-10-09 (the unanswered 06:07 choice)."
+    context: |-
+      The list of design quantities (parameters) has to come from somewhere that does not state answers in advance. One route scans the regulations the project already holds and records the phrases they use. The other builds the list one research topic at a time from that topic's admitted sources.
+    blocks: "Quantity seeding (D-8)."
+    options:
+      - key: codes
+        label: "From the codes held"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "D-8 as written."
+      - key: slugs
+        label: "Slug by slug"

+
+  - id: OR-14
+    gates: false
+    title: Derive a page for an element, such as a ramp?
+    question: "Should a book page for an element (a ramp) be derived from a typed term pointer to its parameters' live determinations, with 'one parameter' as the degenerate case, and never be a container that rows are filed into?"
+    why_yours: "It is the largest optional item, and it answers your repeated question about assembling a ramp as a whole."
+    context: |-
+      A coherent ramp specification needs slope, run, landing, rails, surface and location together. The old item layer used to provide containers for that, and was deleted because a container named for its answer biases every finding filed into it.

+      The proposal is a page assembled on demand from the live determinations of the parameters a ramp points to. It holds no value and no item code of its own.

+    options:

+  - id: OR-15
+    gates: false
+    title: Use held batch-23 material for the inter-rater test?

+    gates: false
+    title: Read the sources already held before fetching more?
+    question: "Should sources already held, inside and outside buckets 1 and 2, be read before more are fetched?"
+    why_yours: "It sets the order of research work."
+    context: |-
+      The project holds sources it has not fully read. Reading them first costs nothing in retrieval and may close gaps that fetching would only widen.
+    blocks: "The scope of the scan work (D-3)."
+    options:

+        label: "Yes, read what we hold first"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "D-3 covers every source that has not been superseded."

+        label: "No, only bucket 1 and 2 jurisdictions"
+        effect: "D-3 is limited to bucket 1 and 2 jurisdictions."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-16)"

+    gates: false
+    title: May the assistant approve vocabulary in bulk?

+    why_yours: "LED-154 delegates adjudication only for enumerated items. Anything beyond them is yours."
+    context: |-
+      Turning observed phrases into aliases and seeding quantity names means approving many terms. Approving each one individually would put a long table in front of you before each mint. You said on 2026-10-14 you had 'no idea what these are' and asked for them to be resolved in a logical manner, which is the delegation this question extends.
+    blocks: "The pace of alias and quantity work (D-4, D-8)."
+    options:

+        label: "Yes, bulk, with me reading the PR"

+        effect: "D-4 and D-8 proceed with the assistant approving and you reading the pull request."

+        label: "No, send each table to me first"
+        effect: "Each D-4 and D-8 approval table comes to you before anything is minted."

+
+  - id: OR-18
+    gates: false
+    title: Are the saved transcripts enough to know which model and effort did the work?
+    question: "Is the preserved transcript record, with model and effort on every assistant message, enough, or must each session record state them?"
+    why_yours: "It sets what a session record must contain."
+    context: |-
+      The database stores no model or effort. The transcripts under transcripts/harness_*/ carry both on every assistant message.
+    blocks: "Reporting for the calibration work (D-5)."
+    options:
+      - key: transcripts
+        label: "Transcripts suffice"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "D-5 derives model and effort from the transcripts."
+      - key: state-them
+        label: "Session records must state them"
+        effect: "Every session record gains 'Model:' and 'Effort:' header lines, a convention last used on 2026-07-25."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-18)"
+
+  - id: OR-19
+    gates: false
+    title: Presume a grey source repeating a code value is an echo?
+    question: "Confirm the rebuttable-presumption shape: a grey source that repeats a code's value is presumed to echo the code, and is not re-tiered?"
+    why_yours: "It affects how independent evidence is counted."
+    context: |-
+      A grey (T3) source stating the same number as a building code may simply be quoting the code. Counting it as independent would overstate agreement.
+    blocks: "The roots tooling (T-8 step 3)."
+    options:
+      - key: "yes"
+        label: "Yes, presume an echo"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "T-8 step 3 applies the presumption. It can be rebutted."
+      - key: "no"
+        label: "No"
+        effect: "T-8 does not apply it."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-19)"
+
+  - id: OR-20
+    gates: false
+    title: Trace standards back to their original studies?
+    question: "Should T4 to T6 anchors be mined backward, for root tracing only?"
+    why_yours: "It amends the research contract's rule R2."
+    context: |-
+      Mining backward follows a standard's citations to find the study its figure came from, so that figures repeated across sources are not counted as independent. The report recommends not doing it now.
+    blocks: "Roots data (D-7)."
+    options:
+      - key: "no"
+        label: "No"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "No change."
+      - key: "yes"
+        label: "Yes"
+        effect: "An amendment of research contract rule R2, and D-7 gains a mining pass."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-20)"
+
+  - id: OR-21
+    gates: false
+    title: Record a direction per lens when a direction is contested?
+    question: "When a direction is contested, should a direction be recorded for each lens?"
+    why_yours: "It would change what 'direction' means."
+    context: |-
+      The query that finds the case where this arises returns nothing today, so nothing is built either way.
+    blocks: "Nothing now."
+    options:
+      - key: when-it-arises
+        label: "Yes, when it first arises"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "Nothing is built now."
+      - key: "no"
+        label: "No"
+        effect: "Nothing is built now."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-21)"
+
+  - id: OR-22
+    gates: false
+    title: What is a floor claim that a study confirms?
+    question: "What kind of determination is a floor claim that a study confirms, when every row of that study is an absence finding?"
+    why_yours: "Your 2026-09-13 ruling says a code value a study confirms is upgraded. Migration 116 holds a regulation-only floor at weak. Neither says what this cell is."
+    context: |-
+      REF-00980 is this case. It reports that it found no grounds to change a requirement, which you ruled on 2026-10-21 supports the tested value. Because all its rows are absences, no finding gives direction, so the cell is not a proxy determination. It is a regulation-only floor claim, and migration 116's rule keeps those at the weak marker, so a confirmation does not lift it.
+
+      The ledger of 2026-10-22 (Correction, item 2) records this as yours to rule. There is no recommendation on record.
+    blocks: "The REF-00980 cell in the first render (S-1). It is left out until you rule."
+    options:
+      - key: stays-weak
+        label: "It stays a regulation-only floor, shown with the study beside it"
+        effect: "No change. The confirming study is displayed but does not lift the marker."
+      - key: lifts
+        label: "A confirmed floor claim reads stronger"
+        effect: "A new kind of determination, or a change to migration 116's rule, so that a confirmation lifts it. Say in the note what marker it should read."
+      - key: other
+        label: "Something else"
+        effect: "Say what in the note."
+    source: "Ledger 2026-10-22, Correction item 2; resolution report section 2 (OR-22)"
+
+  - id: OR-23
+    gates: false
+    title: Confirm: an unretrievable source keeps its tier but earns nothing above weak
+    question: "Confirm tier-system section 8: an unretrievable source keeps its tier and may still anchor, but earns no marker above the empty circle?"
+    why_yours: "The ledger marks the 'keeps its tier and may anchor' half as the assistant's reading of the engine's behaviour, not something you were asked."
+    context: |-
+      You ruled on 2026-10-21 that a source that cannot be retrieved cannot be top tier and reads as ○. What was not put to you is whether it still keeps its tier and may still anchor a determination (decision D-0157).
+    blocks: "Nothing."
+    options:
+      - key: confirm
+        label: "Confirm"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "The text stands as written."
+      - key: other
+        label: "Not as written"
+        effect: "Say what in the note."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-23)"
+
+  - id: OR-24
+    gates: false
+    title: Confirm: 'skimmed' means the extraction method is 'skim'
+    question: "Confirm that 'skimmed' means extraction_method = 'skim'?"
+    why_yours: "It is flagged in the ledger as an assumption."
+    context: |-
+      The ledger (2026-10-09, item 4) marks as an assumption that 'skimmed' means the extraction method 'skim', and no one has confirmed it.
+    blocks: "Nothing."
+    options:
+      - key: confirm
+        label: "Confirm"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "The assumption stands."
+      - key: other
+        label: "Not as written"
+        effect: "Say what in the note."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-24)"
+
+  - id: OR-25
+    gates: false
+    title: Does batch 23's extraction cap carry over to scans?
+    question: "Does batch 23's pilot extraction cap carry over to the scan contract (2026-10-09 ACTION 5)?"
+    why_yours: "The 2026-10-09 recommendation is unratified."
+    context: |-
+      Batch 23 capped how many extractions one pilot batch could write. The 2026-10-09 recommendation, which you have not ratified, is no cap, with one source as the review unit.
+    blocks: "The size of each scan batch (D-3)."
+    options:
+      - key: no-cap
+        label: "No cap. One source is the review unit"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "D-3 batches by source."
+      - key: cap
+        label: "Yes, the cap carries over"
+        effect: "D-3 stops each batch at the cap, which is derived from batch 23's own row count and never typed."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-25)"
+
+  - id: OW-1
+    gates: false
+    title: Does a render stage made of views count as reached?
+    question: "Should the walkability check count a view mapped to the render stage as a member of that stage, so the specification-to-render paths exist?"
+    why_yours: "It changes the rule the walkability script states, and the stage map's own header describes a different shape. No ruling exists."
+    context: |-
+      The render stage has one table that nothing reads. The renderer reads views. For the check to find a path from specification to render, a view would have to count as a member of its stage. That departs from the script's rule ('a view's stages are those of the tables it reads'), and from the pointer-list shape the stage map's header describes.
+
+      The workplan proposes yes because it fits your 2026-08-27 clause that render pulls data across all stages. The report did not decide it.
+    blocks: "The renderer's walkability addition (T-5) and item 6 of the workplan's completion test."
+    options:
+      - key: "yes"
+        label: "Yes, map views to a stage"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "The stage map gains a views key, and walkability counts a mapped view as a member of its stage, with its reads as the edges."
+      - key: "no"
+        label: "No"
+        effect: "No change to the script. The pairs ending at render stay 'NO PATH' and are named residuals, or you design a render table (none is designed)."
+    source: "Workplan section 4 (OW-1; the report's U-7)"
+
+  - id: OW-2
+    gates: false
+    title: Keep the walkability check past the end of the plan?
+    question: "Should walkability.py outlive the instrument and be registered as the stage-pair gate?"
+    why_yours: "It adds a registered check."
+    context: |-
+      The pipeline-state-graph instrument is scheduled to retire at the end of the simplification plan. Walkability is the only measure of whether a stage can be reached from every other.
+    blocks: "Item 7 of the workplan's completion test."
+    options:
+      - key: "yes"
+        label: "Yes, register it"
+        effect: "One registry entry runs walkability.py and fails when a stage pair has no path."
+      - key: "no"
+        label: "No, let it retire"
+        effect: "It leaves with the instrument. Walkability is a command run at the end of each phase."

+queue:
+  - id: withheld_findings
+    title: Findings withheld for you
+    why: "An adversarial review held back its verdict on each of these because the call is the owner's (WITHHELD-FOR-OWNER)."
+    table: adversarial_findings
+    key: finding_id
+    sql: |
+      SELECT finding_id AS id, lens || ' · ' || subject_table || ': ' || substr(claim_attacked, 1, 110) AS label
+        FROM adversarial_findings WHERE verdict = 'WITHHELD-FOR-OWNER' ORDER BY finding_id
+    question: "How do you rule on this finding?"
+    why_yours: "The reviewer withheld its verdict because the call is the owner's."
+    subject: {table_col: subject_table, key_col: subject_key}
+    options:
+      - key: accept
+        label: "Accept it: the finding is right"
+        effect: "I record your ruling in the ledger in your words, and the finding is set to OWNER-RULED. Whatever it says is wrong is corrected in a separate data pull request."
+      - key: reject
+        label: "Reject it: the finding does not hold"
+        effect: "I record your ruling and your reason in the ledger, and the finding is closed as OWNER-RULED. Nothing is changed in the data."
+      - key: provisional
+        label: "Leave it open and disputed"
+        effect: "The finding is set to PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED with your reason. The determination it touches stays provisional."
+      - key: other
+        label: "Something else"
+        effect: "Say what in the note."
+  - id: disputed_findings
+    title: Disputed findings
+    why: "A dispute left each of these provisional. Under the dispute rule (DR-2026-08-19 section 7) a doctrine-level dispute goes to the owner and the rest stand. Which ones need you is for you to say."
+    table: adversarial_findings
+    key: finding_id
+    sql: |
+      SELECT finding_id AS id, lens || ' · ' || coalesce(severity, 'no severity') || ': ' || substr(claim_attacked, 1, 110) AS label
+        FROM adversarial_findings WHERE disposition = 'PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED' ORDER BY finding_id
+    question: "Does this dispute need your ruling?"
+    why_yours: "A dispute caps what the finding touches at provisional. Only you can say it is doctrine-level."
+    subject: {table_col: subject_table, key_col: subject_key}
+    options:
+      - key: stands
+        label: "No, let it stand as disputed"
+        effect: "Nothing changes. The finding stays PROVISIONAL-DISPUTED."
+      - key: rule
+        label: "Yes, I will rule on it"
+        effect: "Put your ruling in the note. I record it in the ledger in your words and set the finding to OWNER-RULED."
+      - key: evidence
+        label: "It needs more evidence first"
+        effect: "It stays open. I add it to the research backlog as a named gap."
+  - id: open_decisions
+    title: Decisions not yet standing
+    why: "Decisions whose status is proposed or deferred rather than active."
+    table: decisions
+    key: decision_id
+    sql: |
+      SELECT decision_id AS id, status || ' · ' || substr(summary, 1, 120) AS label
+        FROM decisions WHERE status <> 'ACTIVE' ORDER BY decision_id
+    question: "What is the standing of this decision?"
+    why_yours: "Ratifying, rejecting or deferring a decision is the owner's call."
+    options:
+      - key: ratify
+        label: "Ratify it (active)"
+        effect: "I record your ruling in the ledger in your words. The decisions table has no verb yet, so its status row is not edited by hand: I file the coverage gap and the status is changed when a verb exists."
+      - key: reject
+        label: "Reject or retire it"
+        effect: "Same: your ruling goes in the ledger now, and the status change waits for a verb."
+      - key: keep
+        label: "Keep it as it is"
+        effect: "No change."
+  - id: open_gates
+    title: Open determination gates
+    why: "A flag raised against a determination that nobody has resolved."
+    table: determination_gates
+    key: gate_id
+    sql: |
+      SELECT gate_id AS id, 'parameter ' || parameter_id || ' · ' || coalesce(identity_code, 'every lens') || ' · ' || verdict AS label
+        FROM v_open_determination_gates ORDER BY gate_id
+    question: "Resolve this gate, or leave it open?"
+    why_yours: "A gate means a determination may rest on the wrong evidence. Its own text names a resolution path."
+    options:
+      - key: open
+        label: "Leave it open until the full text is read"
+        effect: "No change. The gate stays open and the work in its resolution path is scheduled."
+      - key: resolve
+        label: "Resolve it: the abstract overstated"
+        effect: "Put the reason in the note. I run the resolve verb with your reason as its rationale."
+      - key: redetermine
+        label: "Re-determine the cell"
+        effect: "The determination is retired and the engine is run again once the evidence is read."
+  - id: open_follow_ups
+    title: Follow-ups on extracted figures
+    why: "A figure that needs another pass, with the reason it was raised."
+    table: extraction_follow_ups
+    key: follow_up_id
+    sql: |
+      SELECT follow_up_id AS id, 'extraction ' || extraction_id || ': ' || substr(reason, 1, 120) AS label
+        FROM extraction_follow_ups WHERE resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY follow_up_id
+    question: "Do the follow-up pass, or close this follow-up?"
+    why_yours: "Closing a follow-up without the pass accepts the figure as it stands."
+    options:
+      - key: do-it
+        label: "Do the pass"
+        effect: "It is scheduled and stays open."
+      - key: close
+        label: "Close it with a reason"
+        effect: "Put the reason in the note. I run the resolve verb with it."
+  - id: catalogue_names
+    title: Catalogue names awaiting approval
+    why: "Terms minted from the catalogue that carry no approval reference yet."
+    table: terms
+    key: term_id
+    sql: |
+      SELECT term_id AS id, canonical_en || ' · ' || catalogue AS label
+        FROM terms WHERE catalogue IS NOT NULL AND catalogue_approval_ref IS NULL ORDER BY term_id
+    question: "Approve this name?"
+    why_yours: "Whether the assistant may approve names in bulk is OR-17."
+    options:
+      - key: approve
+        label: "Approve it"
+        effect: "I record your approval in the ledger and set the term's approval reference through its verb. If no verb can set it on an existing term, I file the coverage gap."
+      - key: rename
+        label: "Rename it"
+        effect: "Put the name in the note. I run the rename verb with your ruling quoted."
+      - key: reject
+        label: "Reject it"
+        effect: "The term is declined with your reason."
+  - id: unadjudicated_observations
+    title: Phrases observed in sources and not yet judged
+    why: "A source's own wording for a concept, waiting to be matched to a term, declared new, or set aside. Whether the assistant may judge these in bulk is OR-17."
+    table: observed_terms
+    key: observation_id
+    sql: |
+      SELECT o.observation_id AS id, o.language || ' · "' || o.surface_form || '" in ' || o.ref_id AS label
+        FROM observed_terms o
+       WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM term_adjudications a WHERE a.observation_id = o.observation_id)
+       ORDER BY o.observation_id
+    question: "What does this phrase name?"
+    why_yours: "Judging a phrase against the vocabulary is judgment. It is yours unless you delegate it in OR-17."
+    options:
+      - key: names-existing
+        label: "It names a term we have"
+        effect: "Put the term in the note. I record the adjudication NAMES-EXISTING with your rationale."
+      - key: names-new
+        label: "It names something new"
+        effect: "The new term is added first, with its definition for your approval, and then the phrase is recorded as NAMES-NEW pointing to it."
+      - key: not-ours
+        label: "It is not ours"
+        effect: "I record NOT-OURS with your rationale."
+      - key: deferred
+        label: "Defer it"
+        effect: "I record DEFERRED with your rationale. It stays visible."

+# governance/owner-browser.yaml -- what the owner's browser page says about each table, and what it lists as waiting on the owner.
+#
+# READ BY scripts/generate/owner_browser_build.py and nothing else. Everything the page shows that the
+# database can say for itself (tables, columns, keys, pointers, vocabularies, counts, retired rows) is derived
+# from the database; this file holds only the two things it cannot: a plain-language sentence per table, and the
+# short list of queries that count as "waiting on the owner".
+#
+# JUDGED, NOT DERIVED, and named as such (CLAUDE.md rule 8). Both sections were drafted by the assistant on
+# 2026-10-28 for the owner's reading; the owner has not ratified them. The page labels every gloss "drafted, not
+# ratified" until `ratified_on` is set below. The owner's request that this serves is recorded in
+# references/project-standards.md, "Owner statement 2026-10-28".
+#
+# THE FALSIFIER. The build reads the live table list from sqlite_master, not from this file. A table with no gloss
+# and a gloss with no table are each printed by the build, as stage-map.yaml's consumer does for stage ids. A gloss
+# states what a row IS, never a count, a state or a date: those are read from the database when the page opens.
+#
+# THE DECISIONS AND THE QUEUE. Both are written as prompts: a question, why it is the owner's, the full context in
+# plain words, the options with what each one does, and a recommendation only where a source states one. The
+# `decisions` are the questions in the resolution report's decision sheet (scratchpad/session_2026-10-22-pipeline-
+# stress-test/resolution-report-2026-10-22.md section 2) and the workplan's section 4, rewritten for a phone reader;
+# each names its `source`, and the prompt is a draft of those texts, not a second ruling. The `queue` lists the
+# database rows that wait on the owner; each list's `sql` returns an `id` and a one-line `label`, and the page shows
+# the whole row.
+# Membership of the queue is a judgment: a vocabulary value naming the owner matches
+# adversarial_findings.verdict = 'WITHHELD-FOR-OWNER' (waiting), adversarial_findings.disposition = 'OWNER-RULED'
+# (decided) and search_executions.origin = 'owner-supplied' (not a wait), so no pattern over the vocabularies picks
+# the waiting rows. The owner confirms or edits the lists. An answer given on the page is saved in the page's own
+# store and is not a ruling until the ledger entry that quotes it is written (CLAUDE.md rule 0).
+

+# short list of queries that count as "waiting on the owner".
+#
+# JUDGED, NOT DERIVED, and named as such (CLAUDE.md rule 8). Both sections were drafted by the assistant on
+# 2026-10-28 for the owner's reading; the owner has not ratified them. The page labels every gloss "drafted, not
+# ratified" until `ratified_on` is set below. The owner's request that this serves is recorded in
+# references/project-standards.md, "Owner statement 2026-10-28".
+#
+# THE FALSIFIER. The build reads the live table list from sqlite_master, not from this file. A table with no gloss
+# and a gloss with no table are each printed by the build, as stage-map.yaml's consumer does for stage ids. A gloss
+# states what a row IS, never a count, a state or a date: those are read from the database when the page opens.
+#
+# THE DECISIONS AND THE QUEUE. Both are written as prompts: a question, why it is the owner's, the full context in
+# plain words, the options with what each one does, and a recommendation only where a source states one. The
+# `decisions` are the questions in the resolution report's decision sheet (scratchpad/session_2026-10-22-pipeline-
+# stress-test/resolution-report-2026-10-22.md section 2) and the workplan's section 4, rewritten for a phone reader;
+# each names its `source`, and the prompt is a draft of those texts, not a second ruling. The `queue` lists the
+# database rows that wait on the owner; each list's `sql` returns an `id` and a one-line `label`, and the page shows
+# the whole row.
+# Membership of the queue is a judgment: a vocabulary value naming the owner matches
+# adversarial_findings.verdict = 'WITHHELD-FOR-OWNER' (waiting), adversarial_findings.disposition = 'OWNER-RULED'
+# (decided) and search_executions.origin = 'owner-supplied' (not a wait), so no pattern over the vocabularies picks
+# the waiting rows. The owner confirms or edits the lists. An answer given on the page is saved in the page's own
+# store and is not a ruling until the ledger entry that quotes it is written (CLAUDE.md rule 0).

+  observed_terms: "A phrase a source uses for a concept, recorded in the source's own words with where it appears. Not yet judged."
+  parameter_declinations: "Terms considered as design parameters and turned down, with the reason. A declination can be revoked."
+  reasoning_doc_citations: "Claims quoted from older reasoning documents, with the source each one cited."
+  research_code_leads: "Pointers to codes and standards worth fetching (jurisdiction, standard, clause). They say where to look, never what it says."
+  rooms: "The kinds of room and space the guidebook covers, such as a bathroom, bedroom or canteen."
+  search_admissions: "Joins each search to the sources it led to admitting."
+  search_candidates: "Candidate sources a search turned up, and what became of each."
+  search_execution_artefacts: "Pointers to the saved files behind each search, such as the retrieved pages."
+  search_executions: "One logged search: the query as typed, where it ran, how many results came back and how many were admitted. Empty searches are kept."
+  slugs: "The research topics that searches are organised under."
+  source_locators: "Where each known source can be found (DOI, URL, PMID, ISBN, standard number), including leads not yet admitted."

+  specification_source_links: "Which sources a determination rests on, and in what role."

+  supersession_check: "A check that an anchor source is still the best current evidence."
+  term_adjudications: "The decision about an observed phrase: it names an existing term, names a new one, is not ours, or is deferred, with the reason."
+  term_aliases: "Alternative names for each term, by language and jurisdiction, used when searching."
+  terms: "The project's vocabulary: each concept's canonical English name and definition."

+words:
+  - term: parameter
+    meaning: "A design quantity the project gives an answer for, such as the running slope of a ramp or the clear width of a corridor."
+  - term: determination
+    meaning: "The project's answer for one parameter and one lens: a value or range, an evidence marker and a state. The engine computes it from the evidence; nobody types it."
+  - term: lens
+    meaning: "Who or what an answer is for: an identity group (for example wheelchair users), an ICF function code, an access need or a medical condition. A determination has at least one."
+  - term: tiers
+    meaning: "T1 is primary controlled research. Co-1 is lived-experience and participatory work, co-primary with T1. T2 is syntheses. Co-2 is occupational-therapy body guidelines. T3 is grey primary work. T4 to T6 are the regulatory stratum: standards, national frameworks and codes."
+  - term: anchoring
+    meaning: "T1, Co-1, T2 and Co-2 sources can anchor a value. The regulatory stratum (T4 to T6) is walled off from full-strength anchoring."
+  - term: marker
+    meaning: "● confirmed. ◐ policy or standards only. ○ grey, thin, or unverified because the source could not be retrieved."
+  - term: ledger
+    meaning: "references/project-standards.md, the append-only record of your rulings. An answer you give is written there in your words before work that depends on it starts."
+  - term: verb
+    meaning: "A db.py command, the only sanctioned way to change a row. Your decision on a row is carried out by a verb."
+  - term: T-1 to T-8, D-1 to D-8
+    meaning: "Pieces of work in the 2026-10-23 resolution workplan. T-n changes tooling (the engine, the writers, the renderer). D-n writes research data. A prompt says which ones it holds up."

+decisions:
+  - id: OR-1
+    gates: true
+    title: Which figures may feed a determination for a group of people?
+    question: "Should a figure reach a determination only through the lens tags written on that figure, and never through the crossing maps between identity groups, ICF codes and needs?"
+    why_yours: "Decision D-0184 says yes and is adopted with review pending, waiting for you. It is a rule about how evidence reaches people, which is doctrine."
+    context: |-
+      Every figure the project reads from a source is tagged with who it applies to: an identity group, an ICF function code, an access need, a medical condition. A determination is built for one parameter and one lens, for example 'running slope, wheelchair users'.
+
+      D-0184 says a figure counts for a lens only if that lens is written on the figure itself. The alternative walks the crossing maps (identity to ICF to need) to decide which figures apply. D-0184 measured that traversal and rejected it, because it pulls in figures that do not apply.
+
+      In practice, determinations of slope for autistic people, blind people, ADHD, an ICF movement code (d450) and an effort need have no figures written for them yet. Each would read 'pending', with a gap naming the missing lens, instead of borrowing the wheelchair-user figures.
+    blocks: "The lens-routing change (T-3) and lens tagging of existing rows (D-2)."
+    options:
+      - key: "yes"
+        label: "Yes, only the lens tags on the figure"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "T-3 is built as written. Those five determinations read 'pending' with a gap that names the lens. Unblocks T-3 and D-2."
+      - key: "no"
+        label: "No, use the crossing maps"
+        effect: "You state the traversal rule in your own words. D-0184 is recorded as superseded. T-3 then builds the walk over the identity, ICF and need maps, which is more code and the traversal D-0184 rejected."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-1); workplan section 4"

+  - id: OR-1b
+    gates: false
+    title: Does a figure tagged for everyone ('ALL') apply to every group?
+    question: "Should a figure tagged with the identity code ALL reach the determination of every identity group?"
+    why_yours: "It decides whether a statement about everyone counts as evidence about each group."
+    context: |-
+      Some figures carry the identity code ALL. It is a scope marker: the source speaks to everyone, not to a particular group.
+
+      If ALL figures reached every group, a determination for blind people could rest on a figure that was never about blind people. The page would then have to say the value is a statement of scope, not evidence about that group.
+    blocks: "The lens-routing change (T-3)."
+    options:
+      - key: "no"
+        label: "No, ALL reaches only an ALL determination"

+        effect: "ALL figures are used only for a determination whose lens is ALL."

+  - id: OR-2
+    gates: true
+    title: How is a conditional claim shown?
+    question: "Should a determination show conditional claims as branches beside a headline taken only from unconditioned claims, leaving the headline empty when every claim is conditioned?"
+    why_yours: "It changes what a reader sees for a parameter, and the alternatives trade strictness against readability."
+    context: |-
+      A source may state a figure only under a condition, for example 'a steeper slope is allowed if the ramp is under one metre'. Today a code's step table prints as one number, so the condition disappears.
+
+      The proposal keeps each conditional claim as its own branch, shown beside the headline. The headline comes only from claims with no condition. If every claim has a condition, the headline is empty and the branches are all that is shown.
+    blocks: "The conditions change (T-2) and the repair of parameter 3's rows (D-1)."
+    options:
+      - key: branches-empty-headline
+        label: "Branches, and an empty headline when all are conditioned"
+        recommended: true
+        effect: "T-2 is built as written."
+      - key: strictest-branch
+        label: "Branches, and the strictest branch as headline when all are conditioned"
+        effect: "T-2 composes the headline from all governing rows when none is unconditioned, and the note says so."
+      - key: no-branches
+        label: "No branches"
+        effect: "T-2 is not built. The book prints one number for a code's table, as today."
+    source: "Resolution report section 2 (OR-2)"

+    title: May a stored figure be reformatted in place?

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/generate/owner_browser_build.py -- build the owner's browser page.

WHAT THIS IS. One HTML file that opens the guidebook database inside the viewer (sql.js, WebAssembly), so the
owner can read every table, follow every pointer and see what is waiting on them, from a phone. The request and
the owner's answer on the code it adds: references/project-standards.md, "Owner statement 2026-10-28".

WHAT IT INJECTS. The page derives tables, columns, keys, pointers and views from the embedded database. It cannot
derive four things, each read from its single home: the stage of a table (governance/stage-map.yaml), the
vocabularies and CHECK shapes (dbcore.check_values / check_expression), the determinations a source holds up
(dbcore.determinations_resting_on), and the glossary and queue (governance/owner-browser.yaml).

THE OUTPUT IS NEVER COMMITTED. --out inside the repository is refused: a rendered page is not a pipeline object
(workplan T-5, the report's K-13) and the repository's scratchpad/ is committed by rule 6. Publish the file as a
private Artifact. The output is a pure function of the database, the commit and the two YAML files.

USAGE
  python3 scripts/generate/owner_browser_build.py --out /tmp/owner-browser/index.html [--db PATH] [--wasm PATH]
  --db defaults to GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH, else the canonical file (opened read-only). --wasm skips the download.
Exit codes: 0 ok; 2 refused or misconfigured.
"""
import argparse
import base64
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import urllib.request

import yaml

REPO = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO, "scripts"))
import dbcore  # noqa: E402

SQLJS_URL = "https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/sql.js/1.10.3/"
SQLJS_WASM_SHA256 = "d7e61b828523001f26ce0b3f88dabcf6c12e5e6edf80eb4f08b26ac7b946ff88"
MAX_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024  # the Artifact page limit


def load(name):
    with open(os.path.join(REPO, "governance", name), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f)


def meta(conn, db_file):
    stages, owner = load("stage-map.yaml"), load("owner-browser.yaml")
    tables = [t for (t,) in conn.execute(
        "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY 1")]
    vocab, shape = {}, {}
    for t in tables:
        for c in dbcore.columns(conn, t):
            if (v := dbcore.check_values(conn, t, c)):
                vocab.setdefault(t, {})[c] = sorted(v)
            elif (e := dbcore.check_expression(conn, t, c)):
                shape.setdefault(t, {})[c] = e
    refs = [r for (r,) in conn.execute("SELECT ref_id FROM evidence_sources ORDER BY 1")]
    holds = {r: d for r in refs if (d := dbcore.determinations_resting_on(conn, r))}
    for what, bad in (("table with no gloss", set(tables) - set(owner["glossary"])),
                      ("gloss with no table", set(owner["glossary"]) - set(tables)),
                      ("table with no stage", set(tables) - set(stages["tables"]))):
        for t in sorted(bad):
            print(f"owner_browser_build: {what}: {t}", file=sys.stderr)
    order = [s["id"] if isinstance(s, dict) else s for s in load("pipeline-contract.yaml")["stages"]]
    commit = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", REPO, "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
    with open(db_file, "rb") as f:
        sha = hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest()
    return {
        "stamp": {"sha256": sha, "user_version": conn.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0], "commit": commit or "unknown"},
        "stage_order": order + ["infrastructure"], "stage": stages["tables"],
        "stage_judged": {"by": stages["judged_by"], "on": stages["judged_on"]},
        "vocab": vocab, "shape": shape, "holds": holds,
        "glossary": owner["glossary"], "queue": owner["queue"],
        "gloss_status": {k: owner[k] for k in ("drafted_by", "drafted_on", "ratified_by", "ratified_on")},
    }


def wasm_bytes(path):
    if path:
        with open(path, "rb") as f:
            b = f.read()
    else:
        b = urllib.request.urlopen(SQLJS_URL + "sql-wasm.wasm", timeout=60).read()
    if hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest() != SQLJS_WASM_SHA256:
        sys.exit("owner_browser_build: sql-wasm.wasm does not match the pinned sha256")
    return b


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Build the owner's browser page (never into the repository).")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--db")
    ap.add_argument("--wasm")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    out = os.path.realpath(a.out)
    if out == REPO or out.startswith(REPO + os.sep):
        print(f"owner_browser_build: refusing to write inside the repository ({out}); a rendered page is not committed.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    db_file = str(a.db or dbcore.db_path())
    with open(db_file, "rb") as f:
        db_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()
    with open(os.path.join(REPO, "scripts", "generate", "owner_browser.html"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        html = f.read()
    with dbcore.connect(readonly=True, path=db_file) as conn:
        m = json.dumps(meta(conn, db_file), separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).replace("</", "<\\/")
    for token, value in (("__SQLJS_JS__", SQLJS_URL + "sql-wasm.js"), ("__META__", m),
                         ("__WASM_B64__", base64.b64encode(wasm_bytes(a.wasm)).decode()), ("__DB_B64__", db_b64)):
        html = html.replace(token, value, 1)
    if len(html.encode()) > MAX_BYTES:
        print("owner_browser_build: the page exceeds the 16 MB Artifact limit.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out), exist_ok=True)
    with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(html)
    print(f"owner_browser_build: wrote {out} ({len(html.encode())} bytes)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

input.body:
## What

The interface the owner asked for on 2026-10-28 (`references/project-standards.md`, "Owner statement 2026-10-28" and "(second)"): one HTML page that opens the database inside the viewer (sql.js, WebAssembly) so the owner can read every table, follow pointers, see each column's allowed values, and answer the decisions waiting on them, **on a phone**. Tooling only: no migration, no research rows, nothing is written to the database.

- `scripts/generate/owner_browser_build.py` embeds the database and injects what the page cannot derive from it: the stage of each table (`governance/stage-map.yaml`), vocabularies and CHECK rules (`dbcore.check_values`, `check_expression`), determinations resting on each source (`dbcore.determinations_resting_on`), and `governance/owner-browser.yaml`. It refuses to write inside the repository (a rendered page is not committed) and pins the sql.js wasm by sha256.
- `scripts/generate/owner_browser.html` is the app: table index by stage with row counts, an empty flag and the "cannot take a row yet" derivation from CLAUDE.md §4; table, row and view pages; and **Waiting on you**.
- **Waiting on you** (the owner's second statement: decisions "need to be prompts with full context"): each of the 31 decisions in the resolution report's decision sheet and the workplan's §4 (OR-1 to OR-25 with sub-parts, OW-1, OW-2) and each of the 36 database rows the seven lists name opens as a prompt: the question, why it is the owner's, the context in plain words, the options with what each one does, a recommendation only where a source states one, and what it holds up. A row prompt shows the whole row and the row it concerns. A saved answer is kept in the page's own store (the `db` capability, an `answers` collection) and is **not a ruling** until a ledger entry quotes the owner's words; each prompt also gives a line to send in chat.
- `governance/owner-browser.yaml` holds the 56 table glosses, the prompts and the words they rely on. **All of it is drafted by the assistant and unratified**; each prompt names its source and is a rewriting of it, not a second ruling. The page says so.

Everything else shown is derived from the embedded database, so a new table appears with no code edit. The build prints any table with no gloss or no stage.

## Code budget (CLAUDE.md §8)

`git diff --shortstat origin/main -- scripts schemas .github skills ':!scripts/migrations'`: **+685, no offset** (563 html, 122 py). The owner answered "Name the exception" on 2026-10-28 (ledger). `governance/owner-browser.yaml` (852 lines) is outside the measure. No honest deletion exists today: the `graph_audit` set is deleted only if step 4.4's registration condition is met.

## Verification

- Headless Chromium, 400 px touch viewport, three runs of the screens (**29 of 29**: table list and counts equal `sqlite_master` and `select count(*)`, 22 views, stamp equals user_version and sha256 of the file, prompt groups equal the YAML and the queries, one prompt per decision and per waiting row, a row prompt shows long text in full and links to its row, cards, paging, search, a foreign-key value opens the referenced source, a column's allowed values equal its CHECK, no horizontal overflow on home, waiting, a prompt open, table, row and the 97-column table, no console errors) and the answer flow against an in-memory stand-in for the store (**13 of 13**: choose, refuse an option that asks for words when none is given, save with choice, note, prompt id and database stamp, count updates, a later visit reads the answers back, clear). Added-table probe: one extra table in a scratch copy is listed as unmapped with no code change. Canonical `data/guidebook.db` sha256 unchanged. Record and drivers: `scratchpad/session_2026-10-28-owner-review-interface-plan/phase2-verification/`.
- The environment question was settled first: a spike page ran in the owner's own viewer (Android WebView) and stored its result (`spike-result.md`): WebAssembly compiles, the database opens in 19 ms, views recompute after an edit to the in-browser copy, the `db` capability writes.
- `scripts/preflight.sh`: PASS. Two advisory failures are red on untouched `main` and flag nothing in this diff: `retired_vocabulary` (88 occurrences, unchanged by this diff) and `context_map_fresh` (stale since the 2026-10-23 workplan merged; not regenerated here to keep the diff scoped).

## Limits, stated

- The finished page has been seen only in headless Chromium. The owner's viewer has run the engine path (spike) and the `db` write, not this page. Published privately at https://claude.ai/artifact/CwZfTyennssgh7xavU6gmx (version 3). Saving an answer asks the owner for consent on first use.
- The prompts are the assistant's plain-language rewriting of the report and the workplan; any that misstates its source is a defect of the prompt, and the source is the record. Queue membership (seven lists) is a judgment awaiting the owner.
- Pointers with no foreign key are inferred from names and checked against the data; `adversarial_findings.subject_table` / `subject_key` is followed by the queue prompts but is plain values elsewhere.
- A view's "reads" list is the table and view names mentioned in its definition, not a parsed dependency.
- No committed test: the build is a thin composition of `dbcore` helpers and the page is verified end to end above. The drivers are kept in the session record, not under `scripts/`.
- No antagonist pass: the ledger confines adversarial passes to diffs that wrote data or synthesis, and the simplification plan's W7 asks for one on every PR; the record does not resolve that for a tooling-only diff, and the owner has not commissioned one.

## Not in this PR

Edits to table values as proposals applied through the `db.py` verbs (the other half of the owner's first statement), and the ledger entry that turns saved answers into rulings. Both follow the plan in `scratchpad/session_2026-10-28-owner-review-interface-plan/interface-plan.md`. Nothing here lets a page write the database (rule 3).

Done, and the same link now shows it (version 3): https://claude.ai/artifact/CwZfTyennssgh7xavU6gmx

Open **Waiting on you**. It now holds 67 prompts, each opening as a question with its full context:

- **36 database rows**, shown whole, with the row each one concerns.

Each prompt shows:
- the question;
- why it is yours;
- the context in plain words, with any illustration marked as made-up numbers;
- what it holds up;
- the options and what each one does;
- a recommendation, only where a source states one.

A "Words used" section at the top defines the jargon.

- A saved answer is a choice, not a ruling. Tell me "record my answers" and I write it into the ledger in your words.
- Each prompt also gives a line you can send me in chat.

**Please check**
- The prompts are my rewriting of the report and the workplan, not their text. Correct any that misstate their source.
- Each prompt names its source, and the page marks the drafts as unratified.
- The seven row lists are my judgment of what waits on you. Tell me to add, drop or reword one.

**State**
- **Checks:** the screens pass 29 of 29 and the answer flow 13 of 13, in headless Chromium at phone width. The answer flow ran against a stand-in for the store, so saving in your viewer is untested.
- **Pull request:** PR #204 is updated, with +685 lines under `scripts/` and no offset. I unsubscribed again.
- **Ledger:** your two statements, "I'm on mobile tho" and "waiting on me decisions need to be prompts with full context", are recorded in the ledger.
- **Not built:** edits to table values.

  outcome: ADOPTED by owner ruling 2026-09-01.
  rationale: Given in three messages during the lens-architecture investigation: "it is OKAY for a link to be absent in a related taxonomy column", "but a link MUST be tied to at least one", "and ideally it ties into many". Together they are a cardinality rule over the four lenses of D-0170, and they settle a question the schema could not: whether a link row states ONE taxonomy or several. --- 6.4
149:### 6.4 Boundary conditions
165:Two v1 rules survive unchanged and are restated so they are not lost in the marker-system supersession: **an unmarked specification is an error** — every specification sentence carries a marker;
### 6.4 Boundary conditions

Co-1 is co-primary for specification *direction* and *barrier identification*; it is not co-primary for dimensional *values*, which require T1/T2/T3 evidence (or regulatory citation for the code minimum). This boundary is now mechanically expressed twice: by value-directness (a Co-1 source without value-level content grades NOT-FOUND on the value dimension) and by grain (G3: population-grain Co-1 — DPO positions — anchors Population-Mode claims and never overrides an individual's assessed position at Person Mode; `governance/co1-operational.md`).

## 7. Recommendation strength protocol (v2)

### 7.1 Markers — the ●/◐/○ system (canonical per `tier-system.md` §5)

| Marker | Meaning | Strata |
|---|---|---|
| ● | Confirmed evidence base | T1, T2 (sr_meta + standard_eb + co2 streams), T3-clinical, Co-1, Co-2 |
| ◐ | Policy/standards basis only — not primary evidence | T4, T5 |
| ○ | Grey, expert consensus, thin base, unconfirmed, or unverified because the source could not be retrieved | T3-grey, `[EXPERT CONSENSUS]`, `[THIN BASE]`, `[UNSUPPORTED]`, T6, and any source that is `UNVERIFIED` (owner 2026-10-21) |

v1's two-marker system is superseded: it allowed "Tier 4–6 only → ●" with the rationale that "code compliance is inherently evidence-based (the evidence being the code itself)." That rationale is the convergence-laundering failure mode `tier-system.md` §3 names, in its oldest recorded form. ### 3.3 Divergence within `stated` — resolves Q3

**Q3 from A6 handoff:** *A cell with strong Tier 1 OT clinical evidence AND strong Co-1 evidence that diverge — both are "rich" — is currently classified `stated` per T-04. But the divergence is itself an epistemic state needing handling beyond simple `stated`. Does this require a fifth state?*

**Resolution:** No fifth state. The cell is `stated`. The divergence is captured through the convergence assessment (§3.2), not through the state machine.

**Rationale:** The four states encode **evidence sufficiency** — whether enough evidence exists to make a defensible claim. Convergence and divergence encode **evidence agreement** — whether the sources point in the same direction. These are independent questions:

- A cell with converging Tier 1 + Co-1 evidence: `stated`, `convergence_status: convergent`
- A cell with diverging Tier 1 + Co-1 evidence: `stated`, `convergence_status: divergent`
- A cell with Co-1 only: `stated`, `convergence_status: single_axis`
- A cell with Tier 5 only: `provisional`, `convergence_status: single_axis`

Adding a fifth state (`stated_divergent`) would conflate the two questions, making the state machine harder to validate and reason about. A validator checking "is this cell's state correct?" should only need to ask "is the evidence sufficient?" — not also "do the sources agree?" Convergence assessment is a separate validation pass.

**How divergence is handled in practice:**

1. The cell is `stated` (evidence is sufficient from both dimensions).
2. The convergence assessment records `divergent` with the sources and rationale.
3. The Population Mode design range encompasses both findings (per A5 §3.5, Pattern Co-1-D).
4. The synthesis approach specifies which dimension governs the default and why (typically per harm-asymmetry — see project-standards harm-asymmetry rule).
5. Voice pattern Co-1-D renders the divergence in prose.
6. At the Person scale, OT assessment resolves the individual's own functional needs — informed by, but not bounded by, the range — and the divergence at Tier 1 becomes input to person-specific co-design.

**What this resolution preserves:** T-04 is not revised. The four states remain exactly as specified. The convergence assessment is a separate metadata layer that operates alongside the state machine, not within it.

## Owner rulings 2026-10-29 — OR-1, OR-2, OR-3, OR-5 and OR-6 answered

Given in session https://claude.ai/code/session_01Ub36iQ3vbthbsh45LNks6j, in reply to prompts OR-1, OR-2, OR-3, OR-5 and OR-6 of the owner's browser page (`workplan/2026-10-23-pipeline-resolution-workplan.md` section 4; the decision sheet of the 2026-10-22 resolution report), and recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0 and workplan WR-3. Each answer is quoted verbatim. The answers to OR-2 and OR-3 are the option labels the prompts gave.

OR-1:

> "A parameter does not require a lens for each and every disability population or access need. Do not store table rows for parameters when there is a missing lens for a disability population or access need, i.e. for when the parameter is not relevant. In other words, I expect each and every determination to only have rows for the actual relevant lens. Ensure that all relevant codes/identification/lenses are filled out as required, i.e. a determination should never be limited to only one lens because we have different models for discussing disability (ICF, population identity, access needs)--we need to have each model filled out accordingly."

OR-2: "Branches, and an empty headline when all are conditioned"

OR-3: "Yes, reformat in place"

OR-5:

> "Co-1 figures may set a value insofar as the source is academically sound. Otherwise, they set the direction, not the number."

OR-6:

> "Stated and divergent, with a synthesis approach — We make the dispute transparent. We will provide the T1 source as the stated value, but we will note in discussion of the item that it has been disputed by the T2 source."

**What this does.** Five of the six decisions the workplan says gate building are answered; OR-8 is the one left. The readings below are the assistant's and are marked; the owner's words above are the ruling.

1. **OR-1.** Taken from the prompt's "yes": a figure reaches a determination only through the lens tags written on that figure, so D-0184 stands. input.command:
python3 -I - <<'PY'
p = "governance/owner-browser.yaml"
s = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()

OR1C = '''  - id: OR-1c
    gates: true
    title: How does a figure or a determination carry several codes of one model?
    question: "A figure holds one code for each model, yet a fact can concern several codes of one model, such as two ICF codes. How should figures and determinations carry them?"
    why_yours: "Your answer to OR-1 requires every relevant model to be filled out, and the present columns cannot hold more than one code per model. The choice changes the schema."
    context: |-
      Each figure read from a source has four lens columns: identity group, ICF code, access need and medical condition. Each holds one code. A determination has the same four columns and can already fill several at once, for example identity MOB together with the ICF code d450.

      Your answer to OR-1 says a determination should carry every relevant model. The crossing maps show that one identity group relates to several ICF codes: wheelchair users (MOB) map to d410, d420, d450, d455, d460, d465 and more, among them d450 Walking and d465 Moving around using equipment. A single figure about wheelchair users cannot name all of them in its one ICF column.

      D-0184 met the same shape in the old item layer and let one item have several link rows, one for each distinct combination of codes (A-18 by DEAF by AX-AUD beside A-18 by DEAF by AX-SPR), because they were different mechanisms and not duplicates. No source records a preference between the options below.
    blocks: "The lens-routing change (T-3) and lens tagging of existing rows (D-2)."
    options:
      - key: row-per-combination
        label: "One row per combination of codes"
        effect: "The figure is written again for each combination of codes it concerns. It is the simplest for the engine, but the same value and quote are stored more than once, which the 'point, do not copy' rule forbids unless you rule an exception."
      - key: link-table
        label: "A link table: the figure is written once"
        effect: "The figure keeps its value and quote in one place, and a separate table lists every combination of codes it concerns. It is a schema change, shipped in a tooling pull request before any data, and it follows D-0184's move for items."
      - key: primary-code
        label: "One primary code per model on the figure"
        effect: "Each figure names one code per model, the primary one. A reader browsing by another related code does not find the figure unless the crossing maps are used, which D-0184 measured and rejected."
      - key: other
        label: "Something else"
        effect: "Say what in the note."
    source: "Ruling OR-1 of 2026-10-29 (ledger); decisions D-0182 and D-0184"

'''
OR5B = '''  - id: OR-5b
    gates: true
    title: How is 'academically sound' established for a Co-1 source?
    question: "Your ruling lets a Co-1 figure set a value when its source is academically sound. How does the project establish that a source is?"
    why_yours: "The database has no field for academic soundness, so someone has to say what counts and who says it."
    context: |-
      You ruled that a Co-1 figure may set a value insofar as its source is academically sound, and otherwise sets the direction only.

      For each source the database records: whether it is flagged grey, its type (journal article, report, guideline and so on), the kind of Co-1 source (participatory research, DPO position statement, lived-experience publication) and whether it was verified. As of 2026-10-29 the four Co-1 sources are two participatory-research journal articles, one lived-experience publication and one DPO position statement, and none is flagged grey. Re-derive with: select ref_id, co1_source_type, source_type, grey_flag from evidence_sources where evidence_type = 'co1'.

      No source states a preference between the options below.
    blocks: "The agreement change (T-4), step 3."
    options:
      - key: derive
        label: "Derive it: a published academic type that is not grey"
        effect: "No new field. The engine reads the source's type and grey flag. Today the two participatory-research journal articles would set values and the other two would set direction only. A source that is sound by another route, such as a report with a methods section, would not count until you say so. I would list the academic types in the ledger for your approval."
      - key: judge
        label: "Judge each Co-1 source and record it"
        effect: "A new field on the source, set by a verb with a reason, by you or by the assistant for your approval. Soundness is a judgment recorded once per source and not inferred from its type. It needs a schema change and a verb, in a tooling pull request before T-4 step 3."
      - key: other
        label: "Something else"
        effect: "Say what in the note."
    source: "Ruling OR-5 of 2026-10-29 (ledger)"

'''
OR6C = '''  - id: OR-6c
    gates: true
    title: Does 'the T1 source states the value, the T2 dispute is noted' cover every divergence?
    question: "Does your approach, the T1 figure stated and the T2 dispute noted in the item's discussion, apply to every divergence or only to a T1 source against a T2 source?"
    why_yours: "Your sentence gave the approach for one pairing. Other pairings exist, and section 3.3 of the evidence methodology says something different about the design range."
    context: |-
      You chose 'stated and divergent, with a synthesis approach', and gave the approach for a T1 source against a T2 source: the T1 figure is the stated value, and the discussion of the item says the T2 source disputes it.

      Other pairings can diverge: T1 against Co-1, Co-1 against T2, two sources of the same tier, a regulation against a study. Co-1 is co-primary with T1, so neither outranks the other by tier.

      Section 3.3 also says the design range takes in both findings, and that the governing dimension is chosen 'typically per harm-asymmetry'. Until you say otherwise I treat the range as unchanged and the stated value as the T1 figure.
    blocks: "The agreement change (T-4), step 2."
    options:
      - key: t1-t2-only
        label: "Only T1 against T2"
        effect: "Your sentence is the approach for that pairing only. Any other divergence still waits for a synthesis approach written by an Opus-class session, as section 3.3 says."
      - key: different-tiers
        label: "Any divergence between different tiers"
        effect: "The higher tier states the value and the lower tier's dispute is noted. Co-1 against T1, and two sources of the same tier, still wait for an approach."
      - key: other
        label: "Something else"
        effect: "Say what in the note, including whether the design range still takes in the disputing figure."
    source: "Ruling OR-6 of 2026-10-29 (ledger); governance/evidence-methodology.md section 3.3"

'''
def ins_before(anchor, block):
    global s
    assert s.count(anchor) == 1, anchor
    s = s.replace(anchor, block + anchor, 1)
ins_before("  - id: OR-2\n", OR1C)
ins_before("  - id: OR-6\n", OR5B)
ins_before("  - id: OR-6b\n", OR6C)

first = 'Owner rulings 2026-10-29 — '
second = 'Owner rulings 2026-10-29 (second)'
for did, led in (("OR-1", first), ("OR-2", first), ("OR-3", first), ("OR-5", first), ("OR-6", first),
                 ("OR-8", second), ("OR-1b", second), ("OR-4", second), ("OR-6b", second), ("OR-7", second)):
    a = f"  - id: {did}\n    gates: "
    assert s.count(a) == 1, did
    i = s.index(a); j = s.index("\n", s.index("gates:", i)) + 1
    s = s[:j] + f"    answered: {{on: '2026-10-29', ledger: \"{led}\"}}\n" + s[j:]
open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(s)
import yaml
y = yaml.safe_load(s)
print("decisions:", len(y["decisions"]), "answered:", [d["id"] for d in y["decisions"] if d.get("answered")])
print("open gating:", [d["id"] for d in y["decisions"] if d["gates"] and not d.get("answered")])
print("open other:", len([d for d in y["decisions"] if not d["gates"] and not d.get("answered")]))
PY
